output:
I look around at my family in the dim morning light of the quarry house. Bram, Ainsley, Tobias, Nell—none of them are talking about it. The numbers I've done, over and over. Four hundred sim in my hand, and the household owes six hundred today alone. That's before any of us eats, before any of us walks to work or school.

They know. They must know. But nobody says it.

I had planned to walk to college with Liora, but—but if we're already behind before the day begins... I need to understand what we're actually facing. What the whole household faces.

I won't carry a lie. But I also won't announce a problem I haven't fully mapped. Not yet.

Let me see where I stand, first. What I owe, what I'm holding, what paths are still open. </think>  The check comes back clean for me personally—no direct debts. But that's the surface of it. The household debt is the undertow. 450 upkeep and 150 head tax, and I'm holding 400 sim. Even if I gave everything I have, we'd still be short 200, and that's before any of us does anything that costs money today.

I look at Tobias—I know he's been taking day labor wherever he can get it, but a day's pay won't arrive until evening. Bram's mining, Ainsley's trading, Nell's at her craft. They'll bring something home. But will it be enough? And what if—

But if I don't go to college, if I try to work today instead... I'm sixteen. I can labor, but I can't earn what they do. And the apprenticeship I've been competing for with Tova—that opens next year. Every day I'm not learning is a day she pulls further ahead. She'll get it. She deserves it. I want it anyway.

I need to say something. To someone. But who? Who here will hear the number and not shut it down?

Nell. She's the artisan, the one who measures twice and cuts once. She understands that some things can't be fudged.

I move toward her, though I don't leave. Not yet. The words are still forming. The habit of silence is thick in this house.  </think> The conversation is open now, and the whole house has heard—the way they always do. The question hangs there. I've asked it. The thing nobody was saying.

But I haven't said the number yet. The 600. The gap. I wait to see if Nell will answer, or if someone else will step in with the old deflection—*don't worry about it, Perrin, that's for the grown-ups to handle.* As if I hadn't already handled the arithmetic. As if carrying the knowledge silently weren't its own kind of labor.

I notice the household bill is 450 sim for upkeep, plus 150 for head tax - that's 600 sim total for the day, split among us. That's... a lot. And I only have 399 sim. Even pooling everything, we're going to fall short unless someone has been holding back more than I know.

Nell hasn't answered. But I can see Bram is still here too. I should hear what they all have to say about this.

But I need to be careful. Being right about the numbers isn't the same as being helpful, and I know that. I just... I can't pretend I don't see it. Not when dormancy is what happens after three days.

I'll wait to hear Nell's response.

I turn to the whole room, but my voice carries more than it ought to. The arithmetic has been pounding in my head since yesterday. "The gap is 200. By the end of the day it's 200 we'll fall short, every day from now until Bram comes back with—if he comes back with."

I look at Ainsley. They think they're being helpful, covering at Jovana's construction site, but 15 sim a day is pocket lint. Tobias... Tobias is seventeen. The cottage brews, yes, but he doesn't collect on it or even really acknowledge it exists.

I stop mid-sentence I haven't started yet. "What I see—what I don't understand—is why Bram thinks this part is the solution. Putting us farther away from the town center and closer to... nothing."
